relevance.rationale: The standard mathematical account of Seiberg-Witten theory as an algebraically integrable system: the SW differential as a meromorphic 1-form whose periods are the special coordinates, the system realised as the Jacobian fibration of a family of spectral curves of meromorphic Higgs bundles, and the linearity of the period map derived from a complex analogue of the Duistermaat-Heckman theorem. The corpus asserts an abelianisation of exactly this shape and it is currently its weakest link: prop:mi-sw-abelianisation claims the nonabelian multiplicative integral restricted to an exceptional divisor abelianises to the n-th prolonged SW period, its authorNotes record that the Lean was a self-assuming projection and is now a class with NO instance, and it sits upstream of the keystone conj:qdifference-kernel-prolongation-symbol. Its siblings prop:sw-period-residue-sum and prop:jet-sw-tau-decomposition cite only seiberg1994 (a physics paper) for lambda_SW. Spectral-curve abelianisation is the mathematics that statement is reaching for, and it is uncited. Corpus-grep over docs/audits/, content/, computations/, docs/coordination/: no Higgs-bundle or spectral-curve treatment exists anywhere in the tree, so this is a genuine absence rather than a duplicate.

keyResults.statement: A Seiberg-Witten differential is a meromorphic 1-form lambda on the family, characterised by the property that its periods furnish the special local coordinates on the base.
keyResults.useForFolio: Gives lambda_SW a mathematical definition, which prop:sw-period-residue-sum and prop:mi-sw-abelianisation use as a primitive with only seiberg1994 behind it.

keyResults.statement: Linearity of the period map follows from the existence of the SW differential, via a complex analogue of the Duistermaat-Heckman theorem (proved in the paper as an apparently new result).
keyResults.useForFolio: The corpus's jet/prolongation grading treats the period family as decomposing linearly across vertical degrees (prop:jet-sw-tau-decomposition); this is the classical statement of why period maps of such systems are linear, and is the place to check whether the corpus's decomposition inherits it or assumes it.

keyResults.locator: Sect. 3 (Meromorphic Higgs bundles / The spectral curves)
keyResults.statement: The integrable system is the Jacobian fibration of a family of spectral curves of meromorphic Higgs bundles, with the SW differential induced from the tautological action 1-form.
keyResults.useForFolio: This is the classical abelianisation mechanism -- nonabelian Higgs field to a line bundle on the spectral cover -- i.e. the content an instance of the corpus's MISWAbelianisation class would have to exhibit. Explicitly NOT proposed as aid-proof: the corpus's object is a Yekutieli SURFACE-ordered multiplicative integral over an exceptional divisor with a jet filtration, and none of the spectral-curve hypotheses (a curve, a meromorphic Higgs bundle on it, a spectral cover) has been established there.

proposedActions.rationale: The folio asserts an SW abelianisation, uses lambda_SW as a primitive, and cites only a physics paper; the mathematical account it is invoking has no ref() entry.
prop:sw-period-residue-sum treats lambda_SW as a given meromorphic 1-form with poles at branch points; the definition and the period-coordinate property come from here.

State what classical SW abelianisation actually is (spectral curve + Jacobian fibration) next to prop:mi-sw-abelianisation's open class, and list what would have to be checked to transport it: whether the exceptional-divisor restriction produces a spectral cover, and whether a surface-ordered MI reduces to a path-ordered one there. This is the honest alternative to claiming the gap is closed.
